title: Burst reservation smoothing mitigation and customer communications
creator: Maya Thompson
description:
Summary:
A sequence of customer escalations beginning 2026-02-08 exposed an oscillation in reserved-pool burst reservations that allowed short spikes of underprovisioning for small-to-medium tenants. Symptoms included transient 503s and elevated tail latency for burst traffic, followed by overcompensating autoscaler actions that depleted shared burst credits. Impacted customers reported degraded degrade for ~5-15 minute windows during regional traffic surges.

Observed behavior:
- Autoscaler smoothing coefficient was effectively treating recent scale-down events as persistent capacity debt, amplifying subsequent burst consumption rather than smoothing it.
- Small tenants (high cardinality, low sustained utilization) were more likely to be ejected from hot pools during a surge because the controller overestimated the headroom required to protect against replayed burst debt.
- The burst-credit accounting combined with rate-limiter feedback produced a feedback loop: scale-down -> negative smoothing -> conservative allocations -> burst credit drain -> sudden reactive scale-up.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by replay + unit tests):
- A bug in the smoothing implementation applied an exponential backoff factor intended for leader-election jitter into the EWMA smoothing window used by the burst-reservation estimator. This effectively biased the estimator toward treating transient spikes as sustained load.
- Telemetry gaps in per-tenant cool-down counters made recovery detection slow; our detector ignored short rapid recoveries and deferred rewarm for up to 10 minutes.

Immediate mitigation (done 2026-02-12):
- Roll forward config change to reduce smoothing half-life from 5m->45s for dedicated pools (config flag autoscaler.smoothing.half_life_seconds).
- Emergency rule: increase per-tenant minimum burst-credit floor for VIP and enterprise tiers to avoid ejection during transient surges.
- Enabled additional telemetry: per-tenant cool-down counters and a debug metric for "smoothing_bias_ratio" to observe live behavior.

Permanent fix plan:
1) Code fix: Replace the misapplied backoff factor with a tenant-aware EWMA and normalize by observed token-rate variance. Implement safety caps for small-tenancy skew. (PR: runtime#4098)
2) Add unit + integration tests that replay historical incidents and assert no oscillatory allocation patterns.
3) Release runtime-1.21 hotfix with migration hook that recalculates warmup windows for all reserved pools to avoid mass simultaneous rewarm.
4) Add automated detection alert and runbook (pager + Slack escalation path) for smoothing_bias_ratio > 0.8 sustained > 2m.

Customer communications and support playbook:
- Customers confirmed affected: AcmeHealth (high priority), CloudLedger (medium), Two unnamed SMEs. Eng + CS coordinated mapped incident windows and supplied temporary QoS overrides.
- Drafted outbound email and status page blurb focused on mitigation steps, expected timeline for permanent deploy, and temporary recommended retry/backoff settings for customers using client-side rate limiting.

Risks and follow-ups:
- Migration hook must avoid thundering herd; we will stagger 1% rolling recalculation batches over 20m.
- Any change to burst credit floors increases cost pressure; product needs to approve overtime.
- Observatory dashboards must include tenant cardinality heatmaps to detect future small-tenant pathology.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- runtime-1.21 deployed to prod with PR runtime#4098 merged and verified across two regions.
- Regression tests added and passing in CI.
- Post-deploy 72h telemetry shows no recurrence and burst-credit depletion rate reduced by >= 60% during matched traffic windows.
- Customer comms sent and impacts reconciled with CS.
